minutes.headline: Sewer Commission trimmed the FY20 budget but stayed short, and sought a ruling on a charter exemption.
minutes.summary: The commission went line by line through the draft FY20 sewer enterprise budget, which still showed a net deficit. It lowered some lines, asked the business manager to check how revenue ties to Leominster and Fitchburg costs, and debated legal counsel, DPW office rent and the DPW director's share. It also discussed two town charter changes and set aside the Elizabeth Street repair. The only recorded vote was adjournment.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission went line by line through the draft FY20 sewer budget, which still showed a net deficit after the business manager's revised indirect costs.
Members lowered general consulting, set the two infrastructure lines at a middle level, and cut inflow and infiltration remediation over one member's wish for less.
Legal counsel stays at a flat amount paid to the town, with the hourly rate still argued and the DPW director's share of time questioned.
The town manager is to ask town counsel whether excluding sewer from the town manager property clause conflicts with the sewer charter, to be decided before the 13th.
The Elizabeth Street repair was bypassed; higher-payback locations are to be requested and a cost-per-gallon column added. The only recorded vote was adjournment.

why_it_matters: Sewer costs are paid through user charges, so a budget that still shows a deficit points to pressure on sewer rates or on reserves unless revenue or costs change.
The charter question decides who controls sewer property decisions, and the repair prioritising decides where infiltration money is spent.
watch_next: The counsel opinion on the charter exemption, due to be decided before the 13th.
A gallons-based cross-check of revenue against Leominster and Fitchburg costs, and a revised FY20 budget.
